_rationale: This file is the standing exception list for pipeline/clausewitz/roundtrip.py's round-trip
corruption detector (see tests/clausewitz/test_roundtrip.py and
tests/clausewitz/test_roundtrip_full_corpus.py). Read this before adding an entry.
Why the detector compares inter-token adjacency at all: the naive serialiser in
pipeline/clausewitz/serializer.py walks the AST back to text with no knowledge of the
source file's original whitespace, because the AST does not carry it and must not be made
to -- whitespace between tokens is not part of the lossless-AST contract
(spec/00-overview.md). But whether a separator was present at all -- not its quantity or
kind, just its presence -- is the one bit that distinguishes two adjacent tokens from one
glued token, which is exactly the shape of both historical bugs this detector exists to
catch (flag@root wrongly split into flag + @root; a $PARAM$ reference glued onto
preceding identifier text silently split into two items). A comparator that ignores
separator presence entirely -- or, worse, one that tries to reconstruct it by asking
"would this pair still lex as two tokens if concatenated?" -- consults the same tokeniser
that is under test, so a tokeniser bug that wrongly merges or splits a pair reproduces
identically in that question's answer and the corruption sails through undetected. See
pipeline/clausewitz/roundtrip.py's module docstring and
tests/clausewitz/test_roundtrip_detects_mutations.py for the worked proof.
Why this file exists: the AST cannot carry original adjacency (recording it on nodes would
require the parser to track raw inter-token spans purely for round-trip cosmetics, and --
per the same tokeniser-consulted-twice problem above -- would not even be trustworthy if it
did, since the recording pass and the checking pass would still share one tokeniser).
So the naive serialiser is stuck making one fixed formatting choice per construct (e.g.
always emit "{}" for an empty block, always put a space around an operator), and real
source varies both ways in the wild. Every site below was individually reviewed and
confirmed to be exactly that: the source and serialised token at that index have identical
type and text -- nothing was lost, merged, or misattached -- and differ only in whether a
whitespace character preceded the token. Two shapes account for all of them: an empty
block where source has real whitespace between the braces and the serialiser emits "{}"
(the majority), and genuinely zero-width-adjacent source punctuation ("={", "1}", "}}",
a comment glued directly after a brace) where the serialiser inserts a separator the
source never had.
What an entry means and does not mean: an entry says "this exact (file, token_index,
source_token, serialized_token) site was reviewed and is adjacency-only noise, not a
parser bug." It does NOT silence anything else. is_adjacency_only_divergence() in
pipeline/clausewitz/roundtrip.py already refuses to let a check consult this file for a
divergence where type/text/default/safe differ -- only a same-token, presence-only
difference can ever match an entry, structurally, before the entry's own file/index/pair
match is even checked. An entry applies only while the source and serialised token pair at
that exact index still match what is recorded here; if a future tokeniser or serialiser
change makes the pair different (different text, different type, or the divergence
disappearing because the pair now matches), the entry silently stops applying and the site
is treated as a fresh, unreviewed divergence -- which will fail the check, as it should.
Before adding an entry: confirm by hand that the pair genuinely cannot lex differently --
i.e. that no plausible tokeniser bug could produce this exact (type, text) pair on both
sides while corrupting something else about the parse. Do not add an entry just to make a
build green. If you are looking at a real corpus round-trip failure and are tempted to add
an entry so the suite passes: stop, and instead check whether the divergence is adjacency-
only via is_adjacency_only_divergence -- if it is not (a type/text mismatch, or a token
present on only one side), it is a parser bug, and belongs in pipeline/clausewitz/, not
here.
